extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and reporters learning news-meeting reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for writing news stories about hearings, council meetings, conventions, and community gatherings — showing what facts, quotes, and scene details to include and how to present opposing views and procedural outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document official statements and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and attribute concrete numerical facts and official assertions (e.g., 'the Sanitary Bureau had received more than 14,000 complaints', 'inspectors were occupied one-third of their time').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the precise figures and institutional attribution; if an official reads letters or cites totals, quote or paraphrase those numbers to show scale and justify agency actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present stakeholders' arguments and representative quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include direct quotations and representative testimony from affected parties (owners, petitioners, delegates) illustrating how rules affect them (for example, quotes about plot sizes or the seventy-five-foot limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, on-the-record quotes to show impact and emotion; select quotes that summarize a group's central objection or plea and that add human detail to the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe procedural actions and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Record motions, committee referrals, votes, deferrals, and other formal steps taken at meetings and in legislatures (e.g., votes to indorse modifications, committee votes to retain or return bills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State who moved what, which committee holds the bill, how the body voted or deferred action, and any changes adopted — these procedural facts determine next steps and are essential to the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize legislative or ordinance provisions in detail
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting bills or ordinances, list their substantive provisions (e.g., election methods, number and salary of officers, route, stations, clearances, fare limits, profit-sharing terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the concrete terms (salaries, counts, routes, technical specs, deadlines) so readers understand the law's practical effect; include timelines for approvals and required actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain political context and motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why stakeholders support or oppose measures, including political, economic, or patronage motives (e.g., ward politicians opposing reform to protect jobs; party fears about at-large elections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the controlling motives behind actions and opposition, not just surface statements — cite examples (loss of jobs, breaking organizations, party advantage) to illuminate the power dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance opposing viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Give both sides' claims and defenses in contested matters (for example, managers vs. fire-prevention chief on women ushers; Costello supporters vs. transit planners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the principal arguments of each side, name the organizations or officials taking those positions, and include representative quotes so readers can weigh the disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scene-setting and human-interest details for meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the venue, crowd, emotions, interruptions, gestures and local color (packed rooms, groans, laughter, those who could not get a hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set the scene with concise sensory detail and behavior to convey atmosphere; small anecdotes (raising hands, laughter at an exchange) make procedural reports more engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report expert findings with methodology and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering conventions or scientific claims, summarize the expert's findings and the experimental basis, and note limits or reluctance (e.g., Dr. Burns' blood-pressure lie-detection experiments and her unwillingness to testify in court).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the essence of the experiment or basis for the claim, relevant quotations from the expert, and any stated reservations about applications or reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: List resolutions, recommendations, and concrete policy proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: When an association or committee issues recommendations (safety resolutions, railway commission recommendations), enumerate them and give the stated rationale (e.g., ventilation, lighting, water cooler hygiene, Sunday service minimums).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the recommendations verbatim or in summary, explain why they were proposed, and where applicable include supporting statistics or examples cited by the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include technical and operational details in infrastructure stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the operational specifications and contractual terms for public-works measures (route maps, station locations, overhead clearance, power source, construction timetable, tender procedures, franchise compensation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers need the technical specifics to understand effects and trade-offs; include who has first refusal, time limits for acceptance, and stipulations like fare caps or profit shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use narrative devices and humor for human-interest/leisure items
rubrics_metrics.description: For lighter meeting reports (a club disbanding), employ narrative metaphors, playful diagnosis, attendance details and quoted personalities to convey tone and social meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A satirical or humane voice, vote tallies, character sketches and witty remarks help capture why the story matters socially even if it concerns a small group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cultural and community context and voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey the ethnic, occupational, or neighborhood context of participants and reproduce distinctive speech or multilingual elements where relevant (e.g., Yiddish exclamations of old-clothes dealers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include community practices, economic stakes, and representative language or cries when they illuminate motives and make the scene authentic; take care to attribute and translate where necessary.
